title: Smart-seq
scope: Original Ramskold 2012 Smart-seq implementation only, at the assigned mRNA-to-purified-amplified-cDNA schematic boundary. The explanatory mechanism is resolved with the original primary paper; downstream sequencing-library construction and sequencing are contextual interfaces, not additional depicted operations.

evidence.quote: Importantly, Smart-Seq has significantly improved read coverage across transcripts, which enables detailed analyses of alternative splicing and identification of SNPs and mutations.

properties.name: Transcript representation and limits
properties.definition: What biological RNA information this physical cDNA preparation can support in subsequent sequencing, not a claim that sequencing has occurred or every transcript was copied in full.
properties.value: Copied cDNA insert sequences represent poly(A)+ transcripts with improved coverage across transcript bodies and 5′ regions. Subsequent sequencing can support gene/mRNA-isoform expression, alternative-splicing analysis and identification of expressed SNPs or mutations where coverage is adequate. The original assay is not strand-specific, has no early multiplexing, and low-input sampling can lose low-abundance transcripts; full-length representation is not complete recovery of every molecule.

operations.label: Oligo(dT)-primed first-strand synthesis and terminal nucleotide addition
operations.description: Copies poly(A)+ RNA into first-strand cDNA using the tailed oligo(dT) primer, then adds the short non-templated cDNA end depicted as CCC.
operations.mechanism: MMLV reverse transcriptase extends the RNA-hybridized oligo(dT) primer. On reaching the RNA 5′ end its terminal transferase activity adds non-templated nucleotides to the cDNA 3′ end.
operations.information_effect: Transfers transcript sequence into a DNA copy and provides a short terminal interface for template switching. Oligo(dT) priming targets poly(A)+ RNA; the diagram does not depict RNA fragmentation or a separate poly(A)-isolation step.

operations.label: Template switching and second-strand synthesis
operations.description: Extends the first cDNA strand on the SMARTer II A oligo to add an anchor, then uses the anchor-bearing cDNA for second-strand synthesis. This retains the source second-strand block while correcting the role and order of the adapter-associated extension.
operations.mechanism: SMARTer II A base-pairs with the non-templated cDNA end and acts as a new template for the reverse transcriptase. The resulting anchor is a universal priming site for subsequent second-strand synthesis; the oligo is not interpreted as simply a second-strand primer.
operations.information_effect: Adds a universal priming interface to a transcript-derived cDNA strand and enables production of an amplifiable duplex. This supports full-length transcript representation without establishing perfect recovery of every transcript.

corrections.diagram_observation: The orange adapter joins the CCC-end region in a block captioned "Second strand synthesis". The catalogue prose calls the oligonucleotide a primer hybridized to the poly(C) overhang and used for second-strand synthesis.
corrections.primary_statement: SMARTer II A first base-pairs to the added cDNA nucleotides and serves as an extended template. Reverse transcriptase switches to that oligo and extends the first cDNA strand; its resulting anchor subsequently serves as a universal priming site for second-strand synthesis. The composite operation and its output implement this order instead of treating the orange oligo as simply a second-strand primer.
